analysis: Only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py changed (an offline unit test for .github/workflows/ci.yml and the provider-ci-build composite action). No runtime provider, coordinator or key-handling code changed, so threat entries A-001..A-019, TB-002..TB-013 and T-041 are not directly affected. The test file asserts new CI properties: SAVE_CACHES is true only for push to master/dev, and every actions/cache/save step is gated on it, so PRs cannot write caches (this reduces cache-poisoning surface). Checkout pins remain full SHAs. Checkouts use persist-credentials: false, so tokens are not saved into the cached .git. A .git cache is restored and validated with git fsck, with a cold-checkout fallback. Sparse-checkout skips only evidence .gz files and landing mp4s. The tests also assert there are no secrets or continue-on-error in the relevant jobs. The test only reads files and runs git/awk/bash in temp directories and does not execute untrusted input. Unverified, because ci.yml and action.yml are not in this batch: whether the real workflow implements the asserted controls. Restoring .git from a cache populated by master/dev pushes also has residual integrity risk. A poisoned .git or its config could affect later checkouts, though the fsck check and persist-credentials false mitigate it. This is an integration question for the workflow files, not a finding on this test change.
